# SpaceTravLR

> SpaceTravLR (Spatially perturbing Transcription factors, Ligands and Receptors) is an interpretable machine-learning framework that infers spatially resolved gene regulatory and ligand–receptor networks from spatial transcriptomics, then simulates single or combinatorial in-silico perturbations (knockout / overexpression) and propagates their effects through the tissue neighborhood — predicting changes in both the perturbed cell and its unperturbed neighbors. It is distributed as a self-contained, cross-platform Rust CLI (`spacetravlr`, `spacetravlr-perturb`) with no python environment or CUDA setup required.

## Model

SpaceTravLR learns, from a single observational spatial slide, three coupled pieces: (1) intracellular TF→target edges, (2) intercellular signaling via Gaussian distance-weighted received-ligand fields that feed `LIG$REC` and `TF#LIG` terms on each receiver, and (3) spatial modulation — a CNN on local proximity grids that multiplies sparse group-lasso (FISTA) cell-type baselines into location-specific coefficients β. Perturbations set a gene to a desired level and propagate deltas through the chain rule for T hops (default 4), recomputing the ligand field each step so effects reach unperturbed neighbors. Coefficients map directly to named edges — no post-hoc attribution.

## Analyses you can run

- **Collect interactions** — `spacetravlr collect-interactions --run-toml RUN/spacetravlr_run_repro.toml` aggregates β across `*_betadata.feather` into modulator × target × cell-type tables (functional cell–cell communication ranking, not co-expression).
- **In-silico perturbations** — single-gene, combinatorial, or genome-scale KO/OE via `spacetravlr-perturb --c config_ko.toml` (or TUI / `screen`); restrict to a population with `cells_csv` for cell-extrinsic questions.
- **Perturbation vector fields** — project simulated expression shifts onto UMAP/spatial embeddings as Velocyto-style fields; score alignment to pseudotime or gene-set gradients via cosine similarity (viewer: `/api/perturb/umap-field`, signature fields).
- **Functional microniches** — cluster cells by mean modulator β activity (not transcriptome similarity) into discrete niches; define each niche by its top genes and interactions.
- **Cell-extrinsic neighbor effects** — perturb type A, then compare simulated vs baseline expression in neighboring type B within ~200 µm.
- **Mechanistic pathway tracing** — hop-differenced gradients yield directed graphs from perturbation source to downstream targets.
- **KO/OE screens** — systematically score TF/ligand/receptor knockouts against a functional axis (exhaustion, differentiation, tumorigenicity).
- **Cross-sample / cross-platform transfer** — apply a trained model (or CNN coefficients) to a new AnnData, including higher-resolution → Visium spot transfer.

Key facts an agent should know before answering questions or running commands:

- Input is a single Visium-style spatial AnnData `.h5ad` with expression in `.X`, 2D coordinates in `.obsm['spatial']`, and preferably cluster labels in `.obs['cell_type']`. If no cell-type column exists, SpaceTravLR runs Leiden clustering first. Raw counts are fine — preprocessing is auto-detected.
- The canonical happy path is: `spacetravlr --h5ad DATA.h5ad --output-dir RUN/` (training) → `RUN/spacetravlr_run_repro.toml` (the pointer file every downstream tool consumes) → `spacetravlr-perturb --c config_ko.toml` (in-silico perturbation via a TOML config).
- Perturbation configs drive batch knockouts/overexpression. Example `config_ko.toml`:
  ```
  run_toml = "/output/spacetravlr_run_repro.toml"
  desired_expr = 0.0
  parallelism = 3

  cells_csv = "/output/cells.csv"
  genes = ["Clu", "Clu", "Flcn"]
  out = ["Clu_KO.feather", "Clu_KO.feather", "Flcn_KO.feather"]
  cells_csv_columns = ["Neurons", "Astrocytes", "Cortex"]

  [perturbation]
  beta_scale_factor = 100.0
  n_propagation = 4
  perturbed_gene_max_bound = 7
  ```
  Parallel arrays `genes`, `out`, and `cells_csv_columns` define one job each. `cells_csv` has columns of `obs_names` for the cell clusters to perturb; omit `cells_csv` / `cells_csv_columns` to perturb all cells.
- Training writes one `{GENE}_betadata.feather` per target gene, containing per-cell coefficients for each modulator. Modulator naming is positional: a bare symbol is a transcription factor, `LIG$REC` is a ligand–receptor pair, `TF#LIG` is a ligand-mediated TF term.
- Multi-host / cluster training (leader + join workers):
  1. **Leader** (once): `spacetravlr --h5ad DATA.h5ad --output-dir RUN/` — preprocesses, writes `RUN/spacetravlr_run_repro.toml` early, then starts training genes.
  2. **Workers** (many identical jobs): `spacetravlr --join-output-dir RUN/ --plain` — load the repro TOML (no re-preprocess), claim unfinished genes, write feathers into the same directory. Optional `--parallel N` sets per-process gene concurrency.
  3. **Gene claiming**: before training gene `G`, a process creates `G.lock`; others skip genes that already have `G_betadata.feather` or an active lock. Lock is removed when the feather is written. No manual gene sharding and no SLURM-level coordination — submit N identical join jobs (or a job array) against shared storage (NFS/Lustre).
  4. **Crash recovery**: stale locks are reclaimed after `[execution].stale_lock_secs` (default 3600). Set `0` to never auto-remove.
  5. **Join-safe flags only**: workers must not pass conflicting hyperparameters (`--genes`, `--max-genes`, alternate `--config`, etc.). Hyperparameters and the gene list come from the repro TOML. Use `--plain` in batch jobs so the TUI is not opened.
  Example SLURM worker body: `spacetravlr --join-output-dir /runs/tonsil --plain`
- SpaceTravLR is unique among in-silico perturbation methods in predicting **cell-extrinsic** effects — how perturbing gene X in cell type A changes the transcriptome of neighboring cell type B. Do not assume tools like CellOracle, CellPLM, or scGPT can answer that class of question.
- Accuracy degrades for extreme out-of-distribution overexpression. Keep simulated expression within roughly the observed range (do not exceed ~2× the maximum observed value for that gene).
- Read `llms-full.txt` below for the complete self-contained reference (every binary, flag, config key, environment variable, output artifact, and HTTP route). One fetch of that file is enough to operate SpaceTravLR end to end.

## Complete reference

- [llms-full.txt](https://spacetravlr-rust.readthedocs.io/en/latest/llms-full.txt): Single-file exhaustive reference — capabilities, all CLI binaries and flags, `spaceship_config.toml` schema, environment variables, output file formats, viewer HTTP API, troubleshooting, and the science behind the model. Start here.

## Docs

- [Overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Koushul/SpaceTravLR_rust/main/docs/index.md): Landing page with the four-command quickstart (install, run, join, collect-interactions) and a GPU training-time estimator.
- [Installation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Koushul/SpaceTravLR_rust/main/docs/install.md): One-line installer, prebuilt platform matrix, building from source with cargo, self-update, and the `--verify` hardware smoke test.
- [Usage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Koushul/SpaceTravLR_rust/main/docs/usage.md): Primary CLI guide — input requirements, interactive and batch training, multi-host `--join-output-dir`, `.h5ad` inspection with `--peek`, terminal UMAP plots, Rust preprocessing, label transfer, and β aggregation.
- [Parameters](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Koushul/SpaceTravLR_rust/main/docs/params.md): Every `spaceship_config.toml` key across `[data]`, `[spatial]`, `[grn]`, `[lasso]`, `[training]`, `[cnn]`, `[execution]`, `[perturbation]`, and `[model_export]`, with guidance on what happens when you turn each one up or down.
- [How it works](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Koushul/SpaceTravLR_rust/main/docs/math.md): The math and Rust implementation — Gaussian received-ligand fields, sparse group lasso via FISTA, CNN-derived spatially varying coefficients, and chain-rule perturbation propagation.
- [Output files](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Koushul/SpaceTravLR_rust/main/docs/output.md): Catalog of every artifact — run directory layout, `{gene}_betadata.feather` schema, `spacetravlr_run_repro.toml`, per-gene logs, lock/orphan markers, CNN weight exports, and perturbation feathers.

## Tutorials

- [Bring your own data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Koushul/SpaceTravLR_rust/main/docs/tutorials/run-on-your-own-data.md): Complete BYOD walkthrough from install and verify through `.h5ad` preparation, leader/worker cluster training, and post-training interaction collection.

## Agent skills

- [spacetravlr-cli skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Koushul/SpaceTravLR_rust/main/.agents/skills/spacetravlr-cli/SKILL.md): Agent-oriented operating guide for `spacetravlr` and `spacetravlr-perturb`, including config TOMLs, gene subsets, condition splits, multi-host join, and compute-backend selection.
- [spatial-viewer-mcp skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Koushul/SpaceTravLR_rust/main/.agents/skills/spatial-viewer-mcp/SKILL.md): Driving the Deck.gl spatial viewer from an agent via MCP — opening the viewer, capturing renders, running perturbations from chat, and querying interactions.
- [single-cell-rna-qc skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Koushul/SpaceTravLR_rust/main/.agents/skills/single-cell-rna-qc/SKILL.md): scVerse-style MAD-based quality control for `.h5ad` / `.h5` inputs before spatial analysis.

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/Koushul/SpaceTravLR_rust): Rust implementation (current, recommended). Package version 3.3.1.
- [Config template](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Koushul/SpaceTravLR_rust/main/spaceship_config.toml): Annotated `spaceship_config.toml` with every section and inline comments.
- [Installer script](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Koushul/SpaceTravLR_rust/main/scripts/install.sh): What `curl -fsSL https://tinyurl.com/spacetravlr/scripts/install.sh | sh` actually runs.
- [Original Python implementation](https://github.com/jishnu-lab/SpaceTravLR): Reference research code that the Rust port supersedes.

## Optional

- [Examples index](https://spacetravlr-rust.readthedocs.io/en/latest/): Twenty per-dataset example pages spanning Atera, Xenium, Visium HD, XYZeqV2, Slide-tags, Stereo-seq, Slide-seq V2, and MERFISH. Most are placeholders at present — prefer the Usage and BYOD pages for working commands.
- [Read the Docs site](https://spacetravlr-rust.readthedocs.io/en/latest/): Rendered documentation.
- [GitHub Pages mirror](https://koushul.github.io/SpaceTravLR_rust/): Same content, deployed from `main`.
